# Glossary

## System Concepts
<!-- PURPOSE: Define project-specific abstractions that the codebase invented or
     adopted as core vocabulary. These are terms a new team member would not
     understand without context -- they are specific to this project's domain
     model and architecture. Every audience encounters these terms. -->
<!-- EXAMPLE:
**Finding** -- A specific code health issue detected by a scanner agent, recorded
with category, severity, confidence level, and supporting evidence. Findings are
the atomic unit of the health scan pipeline. (All audiences)

**Scan Category** -- A classification bucket for related findings, such as
"orphaned-code" or "circular-deps." Each category has a dedicated scanner agent
that produces findings for that category. (All audiences)

**Health Score** -- A composite metric derived from finding counts weighted by
severity. Ranges from 0 (critical issues) to 100 (no findings). Calculated per
category and rolled up to an overall project score. (All audiences)
-->

## Domain Terms
<!-- PURPOSE: Define business or industry terminology that the project operates
     within. These terms exist outside the project but have specific meaning in
     this context. Readers from different backgrounds may understand these
     differently, so definitions must be precise and project-contextualized. -->
<!-- EXAMPLE:
**Portfolio** -- A collection of investment positions held by a single account,
tracked as a unit for scoring and rebalancing purposes. In Road Runner, a
portfolio maps to one configuration file specifying positions and their scoring
model. (End Users, Developers)

**Rebalancing** -- The process of adjusting position sizes within a portfolio to
align with target allocations after scoring signals indicate drift. Road Runner
generates rebalancing signals but does not execute trades. (End Users, DevOps)

**Risk-Adjusted Return** -- A return metric that accounts for the volatility and
downside risk of a position, expressed as a Sharpe ratio or Sortino ratio.
Used as a factor input to the scoring engine. (End Users, Developers)
-->

## Technical Terms
<!-- PURPOSE: Define implementation-level terms that appear in the codebase and
     documentation. These are programming concepts, library names, or
     architectural patterns that may be unfamiliar to non-developer audiences
     or may have project-specific usage. -->
<!-- EXAMPLE:
**Atomic Write** -- A file write pattern using a temporary file and `os.replace()`
to prevent partial writes. If the process crashes mid-write, the original file
remains intact. Used by all Python scripts that modify JSON files.
(Developers, Agents)

**Subagent** -- An LLM agent spawned by a parent command via the Task tool to
perform a specific, scoped operation. Each scanner category and writer audience
has its own subagent. Subagents receive inputs as file paths and write outputs
to designated locations. (Agents, Developers)

**Frontmatter** -- YAML metadata at the top of a Markdown file, delimited by
`---` lines. Used in agent-audience documentation to provide structured context
(tool name, purpose, allowed operations) that LLM agents can parse reliably.
(Agents, Developers)
-->
